about: LUKE, founded by Thomas and Kristin Vogele with the 2012 vintage, built its name on well-priced Wahluke Slope reds, and with 2018 it released its first reserve wines. Made at Evergreen Family Wines’ winery in Mattawa, which brought LUKE into its portfolio in 2025, the Reserve tier focuses on single top vineyards. This 2018 Syrah was one of the two inaugural reserves, and James Suckling later named it to his “Great Wines of the World” list.

The fruit comes from Stone Tree Vineyard, a celebrated site high on the Wahluke Slope. The wine is 97% Syrah with 2% Mourvèdre and 1% Grenache. Fermentation was spontaneous, with native yeasts, for 18 days in concrete, with about 20% whole clusters. It then aged on its lees in French and American oak, 30% of it new, and was bottled unfined and unfiltered in January 2020. Only 186 cases were made.

Critics found it far deeper than the regular Syrah. Vinous described dark berry, mocha and cured meat with a concentrated, three-dimensional palate and ripe tannins, James Suckling noted black fruit, violets, smoke and dried herbs with a velvety texture, and Wine Enthusiast, who named it an Editors’ Choice, called out dark fruit, smoked meat, coffee and a mineral edge.
facts: Native-yeast fermentation in concrete, about 20% whole cluster
